reports.title: Everpure Announces Third Quarter Fiscal 2027 Financial Results

desk.headline: Revenue up 51% to $1.46bn, beat; full-year revenue and profit guidance raised for a third straight quarter
results: Record quarter: revenue jumped 51% to $1.46bn, well above the $1.33bn analysts expected, and adjusted EPS of $0.86 beat the $0.78 estimate.
Hardware drove the growth: product sales rose 77% to $948m, while subscription services grew 19% to $512m and subscription ARR reached $2.2bn.
Gross margin slipped to 69.2% (adjusted) from 74.1%, but operating margin widened to 23.6% as adjusted operating income rose 76% to $345m.
Cash flow rebounded: $443m from operations and $265m free cash flow; inventory has built up to $379m from $76m at the start of the year.
Bought back about $67m of shares (0.5m shares); cash and investments ended at $1.1bn. The company joined the S&P 500 in September.

guidance.summary: Everpure raised its full-year revenue and operating profit ranges for the third quarter in a row and set a Q4 revenue range of $1.50–1.52bn, about 42–43% growth. It also repeated its preliminary fiscal 2028 outlook.

points: CEO Charles Giancarlo brushed off fears of a slowdown in AI data-centre building, saying Everpure could gain share even in a downturn.
Management expects its hyperscale business to keep winning share whatever happens to data-centre construction or storage media prices; a second top-five hyperscaler design win was announced.
Component costs are expected to stabilise towards year-end but stay high into next year.
The CFO said results beat the top of guidance across core, core AI and newer businesses, and the preliminary FY28 outlook stands.
call.source: Press release (Exhibit 99.1) and call coverage: Investing.com and KuCoin News, 19 Nov 2026 (prepared remarks posted on the company site, not filed with the 8-K)

watch: Whether hyperscaler orders arrive on time to deliver the Q4 range and the $7.0–7.3bn FY28 target.
Gross margin pressure from higher component costs and the shift towards hardware sales.
Subscription growth (19%) lagging product growth (77%), and how inventory and cash flow develop.
